title: Multi-cloud SKU & driver compatibility benchmark notes
content:
Purpose:
This document captures an end-to-end set of exploratory benchmarks comparing A100 / H100 / L40S across multiple cloud SKUs and a sweep of driver + CUDA stack versions. The goal is to identify non-obvious interactions that cause throughput or tail-latency regressions under our inference runtime, and surface pragmatic mitigations for Dedicated and Hosted clusters.

Context / Motivation:
- Previous work focused on single-sku occupancy and kernel utilization; ops has observed customer regressions after cloud image updates (driver bumps) with little root cause.
- We need a compact set of reproducible tests to triage: (1) driver vs CUDA vs kernel scheduling, (2) NVLink/PCIe interconnect impact on multi-GPU batching, and (3) platform image SKU differences (e.g., different NICs or system BIOS tuning applied by cloud vendor images).

High-level hypothesis:
- H100 shows higher single-stream throughput for FP16/quantized kernels but is more sensitive to certain driver/CUDA combinations when concurrent user streams + KV cache eviction patterns exist. A100 is more stable across driver versions but may lose efficiency on short sequence workloads if PCIe throttling occurs. L40S behaves inconsistently depending on cloud SKU firmware (observed on one provider).

Test matrix (summary):
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 40GB, A100 80GB, H100 80GB, L40S
- Cloud SKUs: cloudA.gpu-a100-40, cloudA.gpu-h100-80, cloudB.premium-a100-80, cloudC.l40s-standard (representative names)
- Driver versions: 510.47, 525.85, 535.54, 545.x (where available)
- CUDA toolkits: 11.7, 11.8, 12.1, 12.2
- Kernel/C groups: default, isolate-cpus (affinity), tunings for hugepages on/off
- Workloads: single-stream latency (token-gen), multi-stream throughput (Batched clients with small seq len=64 and long seq len=2048), KV cache heavy (long chat sessions), model sizes: 7B fp16, 70B q4_0, and an internal 13B-8k.
- Repeats: 5 warmup runs + 20 measured runs per config, with nightly, cold-start and warmed cache scenarios.

Test harness and reproducibility notes:
- Harness: runtime-bench harness (github link above) invoking containers with pinned drivers; system-level bootstrap scripts captured in gs://redwood-benchmarks/2025-10-multi-sku/bootstrap.tar.gz
- Measurements: latency p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization reported via nvidia-smi nvlink stats where supported, per-process cudaProfiler metrics (SM utilization, issued_compute, issued_mem), and host-level metrics (NIC, CPU steal, I/O wait).
- Artifact capture: perf traces on 2 representative runs per config using Nsight Systems; kernel logs and dmesg saved. Scripts to replay requests and to seed KV cache available in the linked repo.

Key empirical observations (high-level):
1) Driver/CUDA sensitivity on H100:
   - Pattern: On H100 SKUs running older drivers (<=525.85) with CUDA 11.x compatibility layers, we saw elevated p99 for short-seq single-stream tests (7B fp16) relative to newer stacks.
   - Evidence: Nsight timeline showed periodic 2-5ms stalls attributed to kernel launch serialization on the host side; these coincided with increased syscalls when our allocator hit a boundary (malloc/free churn in the runtime path).
   - Practical impact: 5-12% p99 regression for latency SLOs in our chat endpoint with small batch concurrency.

2) A100 stability but PCIe edge cases:
   - Pattern: A100 SKUs across vendors were generally stable across drivers, but on cloudB premium-a100-80 we saw throughput collapse in long-seq jobs when host NUMA configurations differed from the image baseline.
   - Evidence: Host-level metrics showed imbalance across NUMA nodes and increased CPU-to-GPU DMA latency under heavy batching. Rebooting into a different BIOS tuning image restored throughput.
   - Practical impact: For long-seq throughput-critical workloads, we should capture and validate NUMA topology and recommend a baseline cloud image.

3) L40S variance driven by NIC/firmware differences:
   - Pattern: On cloudC L40S instances, occasional 10-15% GPU utilization dips occurred tied to NIC interrupts and driver versions that enabled enhanced telemetry.
   - Evidence: IRQ storms from the NIC were visible in top/irq stats; after disabling certain telemetry offloads (driver config), dips vanished.
   - Practical impact: L40S fleets must standardize NIC firmware and driver telemetry defaults for predictable performance.

4) Multi-GPU interconnect behavior (NVLink vs PCIe):
   - Pattern: Cross-GPU KV cache sharing and large attention-kernel all-reduce phases benefited from NVLink-enabled instances; performance gaps widened with driver versions that improved NCCL kernel paths (observed in newer 545+ stacks).
   - Evidence: NCCL allreduce times improved 18-32% on H100 NVLink configs when running 545 drivers vs 525, reducing end-to-end tokens/sec variance.
   - Practical impact: For Dedicated clusters expecting heavy multi-GPU serving, prefer NVLink SKUs and test driver stacks that ship NCCL improvements.

5) Cold start vs warmed cache interaction with driver versions:
   - Pattern: Some driver/CUDA combinations produced longer cold start tails (GPU occupancy ramp-up slower) especially with large models and quantized kernels.
   - Evidence: GPU power/temperature ramp correlated with slower kernel dispatch windows on the very first client-facing requests; subsequent runs stabilized.
   - Practical impact: Startup latency SLOs need image-level pre-warm hooks for certain stacks; recommend an init hook that runs a short synthetic sequence on pod startup.

Representative numbers (selected extracts):
- 7B fp16 single-stream (seq64), cloudA H100, driver 525 + CUDA11.8: p50=21ms p95=48ms p99=78ms
- 7B fp16 single-stream (seq64), cloudA H100, driver 545 + CUDA12.2: p50=20ms p95=39ms p99=61ms
- 70B q4_0 throughput (batched 8x seq2048), cloudB A100, driver 535 + CUDA12.1: tokens/sec=14.2k, GPU util=86%
- 70B q4_0 throughput (batched 8x seq2048), cloudB A100, driver 525 + CUDA11.8: tokens/sec=11.1k, GPU util=70% (NUMA imbalance observed)
- L40S short burst (mixed seq), cloudC, driver 535: occasional 10% dips in GPU util correlating with NIC irq bursts

Root causes (post-mortem hypotheses):
- Driver/CUDA stacks contain scheduler and NCCL kernel optimizations that materially affect short-kernel latency and large collective efficiency; older stacks may leave more synchronization on the CPU path.
- Cloud vendor images can introduce host-level variance (NUMA, BIOS, NIC firmware) that masks as GPU regressions at the application layer.
- Our allocator / memory management patterns cause allocator churn that, combined with certain driver versions, adds host-side serialization windows.

Immediate engineering recommendations:
1) Add a pre-merge CI job in runtime-bench for a targeted driver sweep on H100 and A100 (key combos only) to catch regressions in p95/p99 for small-batch latency. Link: github PR above.
2) For Dedicated customer onboarding, capture image metadata (driver, CUDA, NIC firmware, BIOS) and validate against our recommended baseline; block onboarding if image differs on known risky knobs.
3) Implement a lightweight startup pre-warm flow for pods (run 1 short synthetic sequence per model variant) to avoid cold-start tail behaviors on suspect stacks.
4) Add a NUMA/topology validation hook in our instance boot scripts; publish a short checklist for infra/ops.
5) For L40S fleets, lock NIC firmware/drivers or disable telemetry offloads until we can validate across SKUs.

Longer-term investigations / follow-ups:
- Quantify the allocator pattern impact: instrument and replace the hot path allocator in the runtime with a thread-local pool for short-lived allocations; re-run the driver sweep.
- Expand matrix to include cloud vendor BIOS/firmware permutations (collab with vendor infra teams).
- Validate NCCL tuning knobs across driver versions for our multi-GPU allreduce patterns and bake tuned configs into Dedicated images.

Appendix A — quick reproduction steps (short):
1) Checkout runtime-bench repository and bootstrap image: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-bench && ./bootstrap/bootstrap.sh --image cloudA-h100-545 --driver 545 --cuda 12.2
2) Launch harness: ./bin/run_bench --model 7b-fp16 --mode single-stream --seq 64 --repeats 25 --capture nsys
3) Collect: gsutil cp results/* gs://redwood-benchmarks/2025-10-multi-sku/

Appendix B — useful slack/PR refs:
- Slack: #eng-serving-runtime threads: "driver-sweep-oct25" and "cloudb-numa-anomaly"
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-bench/pull/212 (adds NUMA detection checks)

Open questions we still need to answer:
- Which specific micro-kernel changes between 525 -> 535 -> 545 explain the observed kernel serialization on H100? (need to correlate with vendor kernel diffs)
- Are there host OS-level knobs that can be toggled non-disruptively on Dedicated clusters to avoid NUMA imbalances?
- What is the safest minimal driver/CUDA compatibility corridor we can document for Hosted customers with rolling upgrades?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Run the allocator-focused A/B experiment by 2026-02-01 (owner: Marcus)
- Collate Nsight captures and file a short tech-note with visual timelines (owner: Priya)
- Draft onboarding checklist for Dedicated customers (owner: Jonah)

End of notes.
